finding.exact_code: if (!canvas) { showToast('Paint canvas element missing — cannot load', true); return; }
finding.trigger: browsePaintFile starts a source transaction at line 519, then a successful browser Image.onload reaches this early return when #paintCanvas is absent.
finding.impact: _spbSourceLoadPending stays true because this branch never calls _spbSourceLoadResult. The transaction API therefore reports loading indefinitely and isCommitted false, even though the existing document was not changed.
finding.owner_semantics: When prior A is retained and B fails, isCommitted correctly means A is ready under the fresh request generation; this finding is solely the missing settlement, not that B failed.

isolated_alternative.change: Call _spbSourceLoadResult(sourceLoad,false,{error:'Paint canvas element missing — cannot load'}) before the existing toast and return.
isolated_alternative.same_harness_result: PASS: missing-canvas request settles isLoading=false; all other assertions unchanged and pass.

limits: No loaded-app/native acceptance; parent owns that check.
The test extracts real function declarations from the frozen source and supplies mocked host APIs; it does not validate browser-specific scheduling or the installed page's event wiring.
The actual picker callback intentionally returns no result value; assertions use the committed transaction state after its awaited loader resolves.
programmatic_path_observation: loadPaintImageFromPath resolves its Promise after image/canvas work but before the File.arrayBuffer fingerprint settles; harness confirmed isLoading remains true until hashing completes, then isCommitted becomes true. No incorrect identity or stale write was observed. Callers that treat promise resolution as source-proof completion must also check SPBSourceLoadTransaction.
